subject: Escalation Playbook v2 — review + approvals needed by Fri (Feb 13)
body:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Escalation Playbook v2 — review + approvals needed by Fri (Feb 13)

Hi Jasmine / Sean / Elliot,

We’re at the point where we need leadership sign-off on the Escalation Playbook v2 docs before we roll into training + Jira template updates next week.

Request: please review the draft pages below and reply with either (a) Approved, or (b) specific edits by EOD Fri 2/13.

Drafts (Confluence):
- Overview / guiding principles: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=CS-EPV2-OVERVIEW
- Severity matrix + triage criteria: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=CS-EPV2-SEVERITY
- Support + Eng SLAs by tier (self-serve / Dedicated / Private/Enterprise): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=CS-EPV2-SLAS
- Escalation paths + ownership map (who-to-page rules): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=CS-EPV2-OWNERSHIP
- Customer comms templates (investigation/mitigation/monitoring/closure): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=CS-EPV2-COMMS
- Jira support ticket required fields + template guidance: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=CS-EPV2-JIRA-TEMPLATE

Two specific items I need input on:
1) After-hours expectations: we’ve kept the language as “best-effort for self-serve; oncall + incident process for Dedicated/Private/Enterprise when Sev0/Sev1 criteria are met.” Please sanity check.
2) Wording on “time-to-mitigation”: currently targets are tiered and explicitly “target, not guarantee” outside contracted SLAs.

If helpful, the execution sprint umbrella is tracked here: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2841

Thanks,
Dev
—
Dev Patel
Director, Customer Support
Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 11:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation Playbook v2 — review + approvals needed by Fri (Feb 13)

Thanks Dev.

I skimmed ownership + the SLA page. Overall direction is right. A couple notes to prevent paging hygiene regression:

- Please add an explicit “Support escalation ≠ incident” callout in the overview, with a short decision tree (declare incident only when there’s confirmed platform impact or a clear breach risk across customers/regions). Right now it reads like every enterprise ticket could become a page.
- In the ownership map, the “SRE (oncall)” row should say “primary for platform/service health” and “secondary for single-tenant Dedicated unless there’s suspected shared service involvement.”
- For Sev1: we should clarify that “single enterprise customer blocked” triggers engineering engagement, but does not automatically page oncall unless it matches the incident criteria.

I can do a more thorough pass tomorrow morning and leave comments directly in Confluence.

Sean



From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 1:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation Playbook v2 — review + approvals needed by Fri (Feb 13)

+1 to Sean’s callout (Support escalation vs incident) — we should mirror the same phrasing we use on the oncall docs so Support and SRE aren’t reading different definitions.

Docs-specific notes:
- The comms templates look good; can we add a single line reminder in each template: “We’ll share RCA once complete; timeline depends on investigation.” (Helps prevent overpromising.)
- For the SLA table, I suggest we label the columns “targets” vs “contracted SLA (where applicable)”. Otherwise it’ll get copy/pasted externally.
- Once we get approval, Wei/Kira will take the “safe-to-share excerpts” and mirror the relevant parts to Help Center (separate approval needed, per PM-613).

I’ll leave comments on the pages today.

Elliot
—
Elliot Price
Director, Technical Documentation
Redwood Inference



From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation Playbook v2 — review + approvals needed by Fri (Feb 13)

Reviewed the SLA-by-tier page and comms templates.

Requests before I approve:
1) SLA language: please ensure we do not imply contractual commitments in Confluence that exceed what’s in MSAs/SOWs. I’m aligned with “targets” framing + a note that enterprise contract SLAs are the source of truth.
2) For Private/Enterprise, add one sentence about restricted handling (customer identifiers/logs) and routing through the existing security/escalation path when auth/SSO/audit logs are involved.
3) In the customer comms templates, please include guidance on when to suggest mitigations (e.g., region failover, model pin/rollback) vs when to hold until SRE confirms. We’ve had a couple cases where well-intended suggestions caused confusion.

If you incorporate the above, you have my approval.

Jasmine
—
Jasmine Liu
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference



From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 2:06 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation Playbook v2 — review + approvals needed by Fri (Feb 13)

Thanks all — super clear.

I made edits based on your notes:
- Added an explicit “Escalation vs Incident” section in the Overview with a short decision tree + criteria (and linked to the oncall incident process page).
- Tightened SLA table language: “targets” vs “contracted SLA where applicable” + a footer note that contract is source of truth.
- Updated ownership map text to avoid default paging for single-tenant Dedicated issues unless incident criteria met.
- Added restricted handling paragraph for Private/Enterprise and the auth/SSO/audit-log route to Security/Private Deployments.
- Added a “Mitigation suggestions” subsection in comms templates: when safe to suggest (client-side retries/timeouts/stream reconnect), when to wait (region failover/model rollback) until Eng confirms.

Updated pages are the same links (Confluence version history shows changes):
https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=CS-EPV2-OVERVIEW
https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=CS-EPV2-SLAS
https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=CS-EPV2-OWNERSHIP
https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=CS-EPV2-COMMS

Next steps (unless you object):
- Lock content Fri 2/13
- Training run-through Tue 2/17 (Support + CSMs)
- Jira template changes land by Wed 2/18
- Announce rollout in #announcements on Thu 2/19

Also flagging PM tickets for external language + safe-to-share approvals:
- External SLA language confirmation: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PM-612
- Safe-to-share known issues wording: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PM-613

Dev



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 4:38 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation Playbook v2 — review + approvals needed by Fri (Feb 13)

Reviewed the updated pages. The escalation vs incident section is much better and the Sev1 language is now aligned with our oncall posture.

Approved from SRE side.

One small nit: in the ownership map, can you add a note that for suspected “capacity / elevated 5xx / multi-customer,” Support should use incident-bot rather than ad-hoc paging. Otherwise looks good.

Sean
